input: text is an ASCII lowercase string of length n, possibly empty. At most one arbitrary pair of positions may be swapped. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Maximum length of a contiguous single-letter substring obtainable after at most one swap.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Each window contains at most one nonmatching character. Its useful length is capped by the total number of that letter, preventing a nonexistent external replacement. Counters are at most n. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(26*n+26) time/O(26) auxiliary space. Each letter scans a sliding window with monotone left/right endpoints; no modified string is constructed. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
